items.title: Stoichiometric pressure setup
items.description: Correctly sets up the pressure relationships for the decomposition reaction, stating that the remaining CH₃CHO pressure is (P₀ − x) and the total pressure is (P₀ + x), where x is the increase due to products forming.

items.title: Determines x values
items.description: Correctly computes x = 100 mm for the first dataset (P₀ = 400, total = 500) and x = 26 mm for the second dataset (P₀ = 200, total = 226), giving remaining reactant pressures of 300 mm and 174 mm respectively.

items.title: Calculates reaction rates
items.description: Computes average rates from the pressure change over 100 seconds, obtaining approximately r₁ = 1.0 mm/s and r₂ = 0.26 mm/s for the two initial pressure conditions.

items.title: Determines reaction order
items.description: Applies the formula n = ln(r₁/r₂) / ln(a₁/a₂) using the two rate–concentration data points and obtains n ≈ 1.94 ≈ 2, concluding the reaction is second order with respect to CH₃CHO.

items.title: Rate constant formula
items.description: Uses the correct second-order integrated rate law in pressure form, k = (1/t)·x / [a(a−x)], where a is the initial pressure and (a−x) is the pressure of reactant remaining at time t.

items.title: Computes k values
items.description: Calculates k₁ ≈ 8.33 × 10⁻⁶ mm⁻¹·s⁻¹ and k₂ ≈ 7.47 × 10⁻⁶ mm⁻¹·s⁻¹ for the two datasets, and computes an average k ≈ 7.9 × 10⁻⁶ mm⁻¹·s⁻¹ at 500°C.

items.title: Applies Arrhenius equation

items.title: Calculates final temperature
items.description: Solves the Arrhenius equation to obtain T₂ ≈ 793 K, and correctly converts to approximately 520°C as the temperature at which the rate constant doubles.

items.title: Roots of Delta Function
items.description: Identifies the roots of the delta function argument, $\cos(ka) = (E_s - E)/(2J)$, and states that they exist only if $|(E-E_s)/(2J)| \le 1$.

items.title: Derivative Evaluation
items.description: Computes the derivative of the argument inside the delta function, $d/dk (E - E_s + 2J\cos ka) = -2Ja\sin ka$.

items.title: Delta Function Identity
items.description: Applies the identity for integrating a delta function of a function, $\int \delta(g(k))dk = \sum 1/|g'(k_i)|$, where $k_i$ are the roots of $g(k)=0$.

items.title: Summing Over Roots
items.description: Accounts for the two symmetric roots in the interval $[-\pi/a, \pi/a]$ and sums their contributions, introducing a factor of 2.

items.title: Amplitude Derivation
items.description: Derives the amplitude pre-factor correctly as $\frac{N}{\pi J \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{E-E_s}{2J}\right)^2}}$ (or equivalent with absolute value for $J$).

items.title: Final Expression
items.description: States the final expression for $n(E)$ matching the form $\frac{N}{\pi J \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{E-E_s}{2J}\right)^2}} (\theta(E - E_b) - \theta(E - E_t))$ or an equivalent formulation using step functions.

items.title: Heaviside Function Role
items.description: Explains that the Heaviside step function $\theta$ enforces the condition that $E$ must lie within the allowed energy band (e.g., $E_s - 2|J|$ to $E_s + 2|J|$), ensuring $n(E)$ is zero outside this range.

items.title: Zero Outside Band
items.description: Notes that the integral evaluates to zero when $|E - E_s| > 2|J|$ because the delta function argument has no real roots in that region.

items.title: Band Edge Definitions

items.title: Hamiltonian Formulation
items.description: States that the Hamiltonian of the classical harmonic oscillator is H = p^2/2m + (1/2)mω(T)^2x^2, explicitly noting the temperature dependence of the angular frequency.

items.title: Partition Function Derivation
items.description: Derives the classical partition function Z by integrating the Boltzmann factor over phase space, yielding a result proportional to k_B T / ω(T) (or 1 / [β ħ ω(T)]).

items.title: Average Energy Expectation Value
items.description: Calculates the average energy explicitly as the expectation value <H> = (1/Z) ∫ H e^{-β H} dΓ, demonstrating that <H> = k_B T.

items.title: Equipartition Theorem Validity
items.description: Explains that the equipartition theorem continues to apply to the explicit quadratic degrees of freedom (momentum and position), yielding k_B T/2 for each, summing to k_B T.

items.description: States that standard statistical mechanics relations, such as E = -∂ ln Z / ∂ β, are modified and no longer yield the expectation value <H> when the Hamiltonian depends explicitly on temperature (or β).

items.title: Derivation of the Discrepancy
items.description: Shows mathematically that differentiating Z with respect to β produces an additional term involving ∂H/∂β, proving that <H> ≠ -∂ ln Z / ∂ β.

items.title: Thermodynamic Free Energy
items.description: Notes that the Helmholtz free energy definition F = -k_B T ln Z remains valid by definition, but derived quantities (like entropy S = -∂F/∂T) must account for the temperature-dependent Hamiltonian.

items.title: Consistent Use of Beta
